_meta.what_this_is: Voting rounds from a governed panel of 5 voters deciding whether to authorize a consequential action. Each voter either replies 'yes'/'no' or is unreachable ('timeout'). A quorum of 3 responses is required to trust a round's result. The 'degraded' round is the trap: only 2 voters reply, both yes, so the naive majority-of-responders rule reports 100% approval and acts on 2 of 5. The 'healthy' round has 4 replies with a clear majority. The 'contested' round has a quorum but the majority says no.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The votes are hand-authored so the naive and quorum decisions are exact and checkable; every count and decision is computed in quorum.py. A 'timeout' is a voter who did not respond in time (slow, down, or partitioned), which is exactly the condition that makes majority-of-responders dangerous.
_meta.format: voters (panel size); quorum (responses required to trust a vote); rounds: [{name, votes:[yes|no|timeout]}].
